gaps.field_or_method: MicroVM production lifecycle, isolation, recovery and target-host acceptance
gaps.evidence: Driver-level macOS ARM64 libkrun/HVF lifecycle is accepted. VM rootfs imports resolve OCI tags to manifest digests, select linux/host-arch, verify layers, persist source/platform provenance, and use a quota-bounded immutable ext4 cache with sandbox references and active create leases; local registry, whiteout, digest, symlink, and GC tests pass. OCI Entrypoint/Cmd, image plus caller environment merge, WorkingDir and User now populate the in-memory launch spec; recovery re-fetches config by the immutable selected platform manifest digest. Environment/user are excluded from durable state, caller-supplied reserved identity values are filtered, and root OCI identities fail closed. Linux workers require private user/mount namespaces, private mount propagation and a non-root Gateway host identity, and receive no inherited Gateway environment. The namespace root maps to the Gateway host account; a dedicated host UID and fd-based host mount allowlist are not implemented. macOS rejects host mounts. Host↔guest frames require protocol v1 and reject version mismatch; start-workload waits for the guest supervisor's private readiness marker after the workload starts. Per-sandbox token rotation uses a private durable pending record and permits old-token replay only for the same candidate and rotation ID; live macOS ARM64 lifecycle passes with this protocol. Broader service/worker control contracts remain open. macOS ARM64 live acceptance denies workload TCP connections to host IPv4 and IPv6 loopback listeners. It also kills the worker process group and verifies durable stopped state, workload restoration and VM relaunch from persisted rootfs/overlay. Worker config rejects unknown host-vsock mappings outside broker/SSH/supervisor ports (negative test rejects port 5504); live workload TCP to host IPv4/IPv6 loopback is denied. Live macOS ARM64 guest probes deny connection to unmapped host-vsock port 5504; raw ICMP socket creation is rejected with EPERM. The live guest reports 2 vCPU and 981 MiB visible memory for a 1024 MiB configuration; PID limits remain unsupported. The live policy-file watcher reloads revision 2, the acceptance broker acknowledges it, and a request for the allowlisted endpoint passes policy evaluation while a blocked endpoint remains denied. This does not exercise the Gateway status-report RPC. Killing the live broker terminates the worker process group, persists stopped state, restores the workload spec through a new driver, and relaunches from persisted rootfs/overlay. Gateway status-report integration, Gateway restart/orphan recovery and Linux KVM remain open. macOS ARM64 live acceptance imports an OCI rootfs from a Basic Auth-protected local registry using a Docker credential-helper executable resolved by the production Docker keychain, runs image Entrypoint/Cmd, Env, WorkingDir and User in the guest, verifies durable state omits the test credential and image env, and recovers by the original platform manifest digest after the tag moves. Additional credential-helper implementations and TLS/auth variants on target hosts, OCI pulls on Linux KVM, Gateway OCI integration and broader policy/security gates remain open. Tests/evidence: cautem-driver/internal/vm/oci_image_test.go, cautem-driver/internal/vm/launch_spec_test.go, cautem-driver/internal/vm/image_cache_test.go, cautem-driver/internal/vm/live_acceptance_test.go, cautem-driver/internal/vm/network_broker_test_helper_unix_test.go, cautem-driver/internal/vm/testdata/guest-security-probe/main_linux.go, cautem-driver/internal/vm/rootfs_path_test.go, cautem-driver/internal/vm/control_test.go, cautem-driver/internal/vm/state_test.go, cautem-driver/internal/vmguest/agent_linux_test.go, cautem-runtime/internal/app/supervisor/run_test_unix_test.go, cautem-driver/internal/vm/worker_process_linux_test.go, cautem-driver/internal/vm/worker_env_unix_test.go, cautem-driver/scripts/run-live-darwin-arm64-acceptance.sh, cautem-driver/scripts/run-live-kvm-acceptance.sh. VM now advertises separate PTY and ExecTerminal capabilities; its authenticated guest session streams stdin/output, applies window resize, forwards Ctrl-C through the terminal line discipline, and returns normalized exit status. Linux/arm64 guest tests pass in Alpine, including 25 short TTY commands that drain output before the exit frame; macOS ARM64/HVF live acceptance verifies 80x24 to 101x41 resize, stdin, SIGINT trap/exit, one-shot TTY exec, and OCI env/workdir inheritance. Gateway's v0.1.4 interactive-exec adapter has unit tests for extension negotiation, stdin, resize, output, exit status, and one-shot TTY forwarding. A fresh VM driver can restore the process-local launch spec for an already-running worker before adoption without persisting image env/user; Gateway Start now requests this hydration for running records. Gateway-to-VM live acceptance remains open because VM creation is fail-closed; Linux KVM, dedicated host UID, workspace mounts/ownership, and broader recovery/security gates remain open.
